videos.title: AI researcher Jacob Coxon warns what may lie ahead
videos.focus: How frontier AI trajectories affect work, control and public decision making
videos.summary: PBS NewsHour interviews AI researcher Jacob Coxon about rapid capability growth, labor disruption, concentration of power and uncertainty over whether advanced systems remain controllable. The complete interview offers an attributed expert warning rather than a forecast consensus, so readers should compare its assumptions with measured deployment evidence and competing technical views.
videos.why_it_matters: The interview gives leaders a compact risk-review agenda: test capability claims, identify who controls deployment, model labor exposure, define pause conditions and separate plausible near-term operational effects from more speculative long-range scenarios.

videos.title: I'll probably lose my job to AI. Here's why that's OK
videos.focus: How to reason about AI-driven job change without collapsing transition costs into long-run averages
videos.summary: Journalist Megan McArdle argues that technological change can destroy familiar jobs while creating new work and raising living standards, using historical transitions to frame AI anxiety. The talk is an economic argument, not a measured AI labor forecast; its value is the distinction between long-run gains and painful individual transitions.
videos.why_it_matters: Managers can use the talk to pair automation plans with task-level evidence, transition support and new-role design, rather than treating aggregate productivity arguments as sufficient protection for workers facing immediate displacement.

audience_fit.practical_action: Map one bounded recurring workflow into beneath, beside and between scenarios, then choose the smallest role that preserves human ownership of consequential decisions.
audience_fit.review_action: A named workflow owner checks data access, handoffs, escalation triggers, monitoring effects, exception handling and worker impact before approving any pilot expansion.
audience_fit.usable_outcome: A one-page noncoding pilot charter that states the agent role, allowed inputs, human decisions, escalation path, review measures, stop conditions and accountable owner.

complete_compiler_story.headline: Protocol gives document teams cell-level parsing checks
complete_compiler_story.agent_skills_evidence: The source provides a reusable noncoding procedure: download the DPP reference, add it as a Claude Skill or ChatGPT reference, attach the supplied Apple sample page, parse it, confirm 6,485 appears in both expected table cells and verify (565) retains its parentheses before reusing the workflow.

audience_fit.intended_user: Document operations teams, analysts and knowledge managers who review tables, forms and extracted text in Claude or ChatGPT without writing software.
audience_fit.practical_action: Install the reference file, attach the supplied sample page, run the parser and verify two exact table cells plus the parenthesized negative value.
audience_fit.review_action: A document owner compares the parsed output with the source page, records any missing layout or value, and blocks reuse until the checks pass.
audience_fit.usable_outcome: A reusable parsing Skill and a compact verification record containing the sample, expected values, observed cells, discrepancies, corrections and reviewer approval.
